item.title: Handing a 12M/week npm package to an AI for one week — the 5 guardrails worth keeping
item.description: An 11-year-old npm package (wait-on, ~12M weekly downloads) got its first week under a new maintainer run by coding agents: 27 PRs, 6 releases, plus a Rust dual-engine port that passed 496 tests. I ran the key numbers on my own machine — what's worth taking is 5 guardrails, not 'look what AI can do.'

item.title: I Lit Up a TLA+ Model Checker on a Machine That Had No Java
item.description: Claude Code's author claims Opus caught a race condition with TLA+, and the internet is crowing about formal verification. I did the opposite of the hype: on a machine with no root, no desktop, and no preinstalled Java, I manually lit up TLA+'s model checker TLC and wrote my own 40-line lost-update spec. The 2.2MB jar I pulled from GitHub couldn't even recognize textbook stuttering on my box. This post is about exactly how far I actually got, where it broke, and what TLA+ can and can't express — judged against the boundaries I poked at myself.

item.title: On a Box Without an NVIDIA Card, I Tore NVIDIA's Closed Network Apart Down to the Bone
item.description: NVIDIA's DLSS 5 neural rendering network was reimplemented in pure Vulkan, byte-exact at all 75 block boundaries. My machine has no NVIDIA card, so I can't verify the signature GPU-side bit-exact parity. But I shallow-cloned the repo, read the source, cross-checked the 71-block graph, and actually ran one PTX divider regression on my own box — I tore it apart as far as I could tear it, said what I can say, and wrote down flat what I can't.
